1	\section{Analysis}\label{sec:analysis}
2	
3	The four-way ablation in \S\ref{sec:experiments} established that gating produces no measurable benefit over LoRA-only fine-tuning. This section investigates why. We first characterize the gradient dynamics between the two training objectives (\S\ref{subsec:gradient-conflict}), then show that the learned gates exhibit behavior opposite to the design intent (\S\ref{subsec:gate-conditioning}). A targeted causal experiment rules out gradient direction conflict as the explanation (\S\ref{subsec:pcgrad}), and a distribution shift analysis identifies the actual failure mode (\S\ref{subsec:dist-shift}).
4	
5	\subsection{Gradient Conflict Observation}\label{subsec:gradient-conflict}
6	
7	To understand how the two loss terms interact during training, we measure the cosine similarity between $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ and $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ at each transformer layer across three training epochs. Table~\ref{tab:grad-conflict} summarizes the results.
8	
9	\begin{table}[t]
10	\centering
11	\small
12	\caption{Gradient interaction between $\mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ and $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ across training epochs. \textit{cos\_sim}: mean cosine similarity across layers. \textit{neg\%}: percentage of layers with negative cosine similarity. \textit{mag\_ratio}: ratio of NTP to GAR gradient magnitudes.}
13	\label{tab:grad-conflict}
14	\begin{tabular}{lccc}
15	\toprule
16	\textbf{Epoch} & \textbf{cos\_sim} & \textbf{neg\%} & \textbf{mag\_ratio} \\
17	\midrule
18	0 & $-$0.089 & 78.6 & 7.5$\times$ \\
19	1 & $-$0.054 & 71.4 & 13.7$\times$ \\
20	2 & $-$0.042 & 67.9 & 14.7$\times$ \\
21	\bottomrule
22	\end{tabular}
23	\end{table}
24	
25	Two patterns are apparent. First, the NTP and GAR gradients point in opposing directions across 68--79\% of layers throughout training. The mean cosine similarity is negative at every epoch, though it attenuates slightly from $-$0.089 to $-$0.042 as training progresses. Second, the NTP gradient magnitude dominates the GAR gradient by a factor that grows from 7.5$\times$ at epoch~0 to 14.7$\times$ at epoch~2. Direction conflict decreases while magnitude imbalance worsens. We observe these patterns as descriptive statistics of the training dynamics. This does not establish that gradient conflict causes $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ to fail; \S\ref{subsec:pcgrad} tests this hypothesis directly.
26	
27	\subsection{Gate Turn Conditioning}\label{subsec:gate-conditioning}
28	
29	The design intent of ThreadGate is to modulate the residual stream more aggressively at late conversation turns, where GAR naturally decays (\S\ref{sec:background}). \section{Analysis}\label{sec:analysis}

We first characterize the gradient dynamics between the two training objectives (\S\ref{subsec:gradient-conflict}), then show that the learned gates exhibit behavior opposite to the design intent (\S\ref{subsec:gate-conditioning}). A targeted causal experiment rules out gradient direction conflict as the explanation (\S\ref{subsec:pcgrad}), and a distribution shift analysis identifies the actual failure mode (\S\ref{subsec:dist-shift}).

\subsection{Gradient Conflict Observation}\label{subsec:gradient-conflict}

To understand how the two loss terms interact during training, we measure the cosine similarity between $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ and $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ at each transformer layer across three training epochs. Table~\ref{tab:grad-conflict} summarizes the results.

\centering

\label{tab:grad-conflict}
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Epoch} & \textbf{cos\_sim} & \textbf{neg\%} & \textbf{mag\_ratio} \\
\midrule
0 & $-$0.089 & 78.6 & 7.5$\times$ \\
1 & $-$0.054 & 71.4 & 13.7$\times$ \\
2 & $-$0.042 & 67.9 & 14.7$\times$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The mean cosine similarity is negative at every epoch, though it attenuates slightly from $-$0.089 to $-$0.042 as training progresses. Second, the NTP gradient magnitude dominates the GAR gradient by a factor that grows from 7.5$\times$ at epoch~0 to 14.7$\times$ at epoch~2. Direction conflict decreases while magnitude imbalance worsens. We observe these patterns as descriptive statistics of the training dynamics. \section{Analysis}\label{sec:analysis}

The four-way ablation in \S\ref{sec:experiments} established that gating produces no measurable benefit over LoRA-only fine-tuning. This section investigates why. We first characterize the gradient dynamics between the two training objectives (\S\ref{subsec:gradient-conflict}), then show that the learned gates exhibit behavior opposite to the design intent (\S\ref{subsec:gate-conditioning}). A targeted causal experiment rules out gradient direction conflict as the explanation (\S\ref{subsec:pcgrad}), and a distribution shift analysis identifies the actual failure mode (\S\ref{subsec:dist-shift}).

\subsection{Gradient Conflict Observation}\label{subsec:gradient-conflict}

To understand how the two loss terms interact during training, we measure the cosine similarity between $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ and $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ at each transformer layer across three training epochs. Table~\ref{tab:grad-conflict} summarizes the results.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Gradient interaction between $\mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ and $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ across training epochs. \textit{cos\_sim}: mean cosine similarity across layers. \textit{neg\%}: percentage of layers with negative cosine similarity. \textit{mag\_ratio}: ratio of NTP to GAR gradient magnitudes.}
\label{tab:grad-conflict}
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Epoch} & \textbf{cos\_sim} & \textbf{neg\%} & \textbf{mag\_ratio} \\
\midrule
0 & $-$0.089 & 78.6 & 7.5$\times$ \\
1 & $-$0.054 & 71.4 & 13.7$\times$ \\
2 & $-$0.042 & 67.9 & 14.7$\times$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Two patterns are apparent. First, the NTP and GAR gradients point in opposing directions across 68--79\% of layers throughout training. The mean cosine similarity is negative at every epoch, though it attenuates slightly from $-$0.089 to $-$0.042 as training progresses. Second, the NTP gradient magnitude dominates the GAR gradient by a factor that grows from 7.5$\times$ at epoch~0 to 14.7$\times$ at epoch~2. Direction conflict decreases while magnitude imbalance worsens. We observe these patterns as descriptive statistics of the training dynamics. This does not establish that gradient conflict causes $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ to fail; \S\ref{subsec:pcgrad} tests this hypothesis directly.

\subsection{Gate Turn Conditioning}\label{subsec:gate-conditioning}

The design intent of ThreadGate is to modulate the residual stream more aggressively at late conversation turns, where GAR naturally decays (\S\ref{sec:background}). We test whether the learned gates achieve this by comparing gate values at turn~1 (early) and turn~21 (late) across all 28 layers of the trained model.

The gates do the opposite. In 27 of 28 layers, the gate value at turn~1 is lower than at turn~21 (Wilcoxon signed-rank test: $p = 3.73 \times 10^{-8}$, effect size $r = 0.975$). At layer~23, the gate is 0.769 at turn~1 and 0.979 at turn~21; at layer~14, it is 0.747 at turn~1 and 0.928 at turn~21. The pattern is consistent: gates suppress the residual stream more at early turns (where GAR is already high) and become nearly passive at late turns (where intervention is most needed). This inversion has a straightforward explanation. NTP loss pressure is highest at late turns, where the model must predict tokens conditioned on a long context. The NTP gradient pushes gates toward 1.0 to preserve the full sublayer computation, and this pressure is strongest precisely where GAR-based attenuation would be most useful.

The practical consequence is that the gates provide almost no intervention at inference time. Across all layers, mean gate values during inference range from 0.93 to 0.98, corresponding to residual stream attenuation of only 2--7\%. This attenuation is far below what would be required for meaningful modulation, and it explains the convergence with LoRA-only in Table~\ref{tab:four-way}. Figure~\ref{fig:gate-shift}(a) visualizes the per-layer gate difference between early and late turns.

\subsection{PCGrad Causal Exclusion}\label{subsec:pcgrad}

The gradient conflict observed in \S\ref{subsec:gradient-conflict} raises a natural hypothesis: perhaps the opposing gradient directions between $\mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ and $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ prevent the GAR objective from converging. If direction conflict is the cause of $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ collapse, then eliminating direction conflict should prevent the collapse. We test this prediction using PCGrad \citep{yu2020pcgrad}.

PCGrad projects the gradient of one task onto the normal plane of the other whenever two task gradients conflict in direction. We apply PCGrad to the gate parameters only, projecting $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ onto the orthogonal complement of $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ whenever their cosine similarity is negative. This eliminates the directional component of the conflict while leaving magnitude differences intact. PCGrad does not address magnitude imbalance (which GradNorm targets; \citealp{chen2018gradnorm}) or Nash equilibrium violations (which Nash-MTL targets; \citealp{navon2022nash}); our claim is scoped to direction conflict alone.

The result is unambiguous. Under PCGrad, the cosine similarity between NTP and GAR gradients on gate parameters turns positive by gradient step~200 ($+$0.086), confirming that PCGrad successfully removes direction conflict. Yet $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ follows a trajectory nearly identical to the baseline (v7) and collapses in the same manner. Figure~\ref{fig:training-pcgrad}(b) overlays the $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ training curves for both conditions.

The causal exclusion follows by \emph{modus tollens}:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If direction conflict causes $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ collapse, then removing direction conflict should prevent the collapse.
    \item PCGrad removes direction conflict (cosine similarity turns positive at step~200).
    \item $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ collapses regardless.
    \item Therefore, direction conflict is not the cause of $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ collapse.
\end{enumerate}

This result recharacterizes the gradient observations in \S\ref{subsec:gradient-conflict}: direction conflict between $\mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ and $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ is a symptom of the multi-objective optimization dynamics, not the mechanism responsible for GAR failure. The magnitude imbalance (7.5--14.7$\times$) and potential Nash equilibrium violations remain as candidate explanations that future work can test with GradNorm \citep{chen2018gradnorm} and Nash-MTL \citep{navon2022nash}.

\subsection{Distribution Shift Analysis}\label{subsec:dist-shift}

The preceding subsections explain why the gating mechanism is ineffective during training. This subsection addresses why the learned GAR improvements fail to transfer from training to inference.

Recall from \S\ref{sec:experiments} that teacher-forced GAR-ours reaches 0.49 for all fine-tuned variants, while autoregressive GAR-ours drops to 0.016, a 30$\times$ gap. We decompose this gap by comparing same-distribution and cross-distribution evaluation. Under same-distribution evaluation (teacher-forced UltraChat text), GAR-ours is approximately 0.49, confirming that the model has learned the intended attention pattern on the training distribution. Under cross-distribution evaluation (model-generated text), GAR-ours drops to 0.016. The training itself is sound; the failure is one of generalization.

GAR-Dongre provides a revealing control. Across both evaluation conditions, GAR-Dongre remains uniformly low (0.01--0.02) with no distribution gap. The distribution shift selectively destroys the concentrated attention pattern captured by GAR-ours (last-token, summary-position attention) while leaving the diffuse attention pattern captured by GAR-Dongre (averaged across all positions) unaffected. This selectivity implies that the distribution shift disrupts a specific learned routing behavior rather than attention computation in general.

The mechanism connecting training regime to distribution shift is exposure bias \citep{bengio2015scheduled}. During training, the model conditions each token prediction on ground-truth prefixes from UltraChat. At inference, it conditions on its own prior outputs. The attention patterns optimized for the former distribution do not transfer to the latter, because the statistical properties of model-generated text diverge from those of human-written reference text. The 2--7\% gate attenuation documented in \S\ref{subsec:gate-conditioning} is far too weak to compensate for this distributional mismatch.

\citet{he2019exposure} showed that language models exhibit token-level self-recovery from exposure bias: accumulated errors in autoregressive generation do not degrade perplexity as severely as worst-case analysis predicts. Our results are consistent with this finding at the token level, as PPL remains normal across all conditions (Table~\ref{tab:four-way}). The critical distinction is between primary and auxiliary objectives. The NTP objective is robust to exposure bias because next-token prediction is the same task at both training and inference time. The GAR auxiliary objective is fragile because it optimizes an attention pattern under teacher-forced context that has no counterpart in autoregressive generation. Primary-task self-recovery does not extend to auxiliary objectives that depend on distributional properties of the input prefix. Figure~\ref{fig:gate-shift}(b) summarizes the four-model GAR comparison across evaluation conditions.

\section{Analysis}\label{sec:analysis}

The four-way ablation in \S\ref{sec:experiments} established that gating produces no measurable benefit over LoRA-only fine-tuning. This section investigates why. We first characterize the gradient dynamics between the two training objectives (\S\ref{subsec:gradient-conflict}), then show that the learned gates exhibit behavior opposite to the design intent (\S\ref{subsec:gate-conditioning}). A targeted causal experiment rules out gradient direction conflict as the explanation (\S\ref{subsec:pcgrad}), and a distribution shift analysis identifies the actual failure mode (\S\ref{subsec:dist-shift}).

\subsection{Gradient Conflict Observation}\label{subsec:gradient-conflict}

To understand how the two loss terms interact during training, we measure the cosine similarity between $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ and $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ at each transformer layer across three training epochs. Table~\ref{tab:grad-conflict} summarizes the results.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Gradient interaction between $\mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ and $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ across training epochs. \textit{cos\_sim}: mean cosine similarity across layers. \textit{neg\%}: percentage of layers with negative cosine similarity. \textit{mag\_ratio}: ratio of NTP to GAR gradient magnitudes.}
\label{tab:grad-conflict}
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Epoch} & \textbf{cos\_sim} & \textbf{neg\%} & \textbf{mag\_ratio} \\
\midrule
0 & $-$0.089 & 78.6 & 7.5$\times$ \\
1 & $-$0.054 & 71.4 & 13.7$\times$ \\
2 & $-$0.042 & 67.9 & 14.7$\times$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Two patterns are apparent. First, the NTP and GAR gradients point in opposing directions across 68--79\% of layers throughout training. The mean cosine similarity is negative at every epoch, though it attenuates slightly from $-$0.089 to $-$0.042 as training progresses. Second, the NTP gradient magnitude dominates the GAR gradient by a factor that grows from 7.5$\times$ at epoch~0 to 14.7$\times$ at epoch~2. Direction conflict decreases while magnitude imbalance worsens. We observe these patterns as descriptive statistics of the training dynamics. This does not establish that gradient conflict causes $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ to fail; \S\ref{subsec:pcgrad} tests this hypothesis directly.

\subsection{Gate Turn Conditioning}\label{subsec:gate-conditioning}

The design intent of ThreadGate is to modulate the residual stream more aggressively at late conversation turns, where GAR naturally decays (\S\ref{sec:background}). We test whether the learned gates achieve this by comparing gate values at turn~1 (early) and turn~21 (late) across all 28 layers of the trained model.

The gates do the opposite. In 27 of 28 layers, the gate value at turn~1 is lower than at turn~21 (Wilcoxon signed-rank test: $p = 3.73 \times 10^{-8}$, effect size $r = 0.975$). At layer~23, the gate is 0.769 at turn~1 and 0.979 at turn~21; at layer~14, it is 0.747 at turn~1 and 0.928 at turn~21. The pattern is consistent: gates suppress the residual stream more at early turns (where GAR is already high) and become nearly passive at late turns (where intervention is most needed). This inversion has a straightforward explanation. NTP loss pressure is highest at late turns, where the model must predict tokens conditioned on a long context. The NTP gradient pushes gates toward 1.0 to preserve the full sublayer computation, and this pressure is strongest precisely where GAR-based attenuation would be most useful.

The practical consequence is that the gates provide almost no intervention at inference time. Across all layers, mean gate values during inference range from 0.93 to 0.98, corresponding to residual stream attenuation of only 2--7\%. This attenuation is far below what would be required for meaningful modulation, and it explains the convergence with LoRA-only in Table~\ref{tab:four-way}. Figure~\ref{fig:gate-shift}(a) visualizes the per-layer gate difference between early and late turns.

\subsection{PCGrad Causal Exclusion}\label{subsec:pcgrad}

The gradient conflict observed in \S\ref{subsec:gradient-conflict} raises a natural hypothesis: perhaps the opposing gradient directions between $\mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ and $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ prevent the GAR objective from converging. If direction conflict is the cause of $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ collapse, then eliminating direction conflict should prevent the collapse. We test this prediction using PCGrad \citep{yu2020pcgrad}.

PCGrad projects the gradient of one task onto the normal plane of the other whenever two task gradients conflict in direction. We apply PCGrad to the gate parameters only, projecting $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ onto the orthogonal complement of $\nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ whenever their cosine similarity is negative. This eliminates the directional component of the conflict while leaving magnitude differences intact. PCGrad does not address magnitude imbalance (which GradNorm targets; \citealp{chen2018gradnorm}) or Nash equilibrium violations (which Nash-MTL targets; \citealp{navon2022nash}); our claim is scoped to direction conflict alone.

The result is unambiguous. Under PCGrad, the cosine similarity between NTP and GAR gradients on gate parameters turns positive by gradient step~200 ($+$0.086), confirming that PCGrad successfully removes direction conflict. Yet $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ follows a trajectory nearly identical to the baseline (v7) and collapses in the same manner. Figure~\ref{fig:training-pcgrad}(b) overlays the $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ training curves for both conditions.

The causal exclusion follows by \emph{modus tollens}:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If direction conflict causes $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ collapse, then removing direction conflict should prevent the collapse.
    \item PCGrad removes direction conflict (cosine similarity turns positive at step~200).
    \item $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ collapses regardless.
    \item Therefore, direction conflict is not the cause of $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ collapse.
\end{enumerate}

This result recharacterizes the gradient observations in \S\ref{subsec:gradient-conflict}: direction conflict between $\mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ and $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ is a symptom of the multi-objective optimization dynamics, not the mechanism responsible for GAR failure. The magnitude imbalance (7.5--14.7$\times$) and potential Nash equilibrium violations remain as candidate explanations that future work can test with GradNorm \citep{chen2018gradnorm} and Nash-MTL \citep{navon2022nash}.

\subsection{Distribution Shift Analysis}\label{subsec:dist-shift}

The preceding subsections explain why the gating mechanism is ineffective during training. This subsection addresses why the learned GAR improvements fail to transfer from training to inference.

Recall from \S\ref{sec:experiments} that teacher-forced GAR-ours reaches 0.49 for all fine-tuned variants, while autoregressive GAR-ours drops to 0.016, a 30$\times$ gap. We decompose this gap by comparing same-distribution and cross-distribution evaluation. Under same-distribution evaluation (teacher-forced UltraChat text), GAR-ours is approximately 0.49, confirming that the model has learned the intended attention pattern on the training distribution. Under cross-distribution evaluation (model-generated text), GAR-ours drops to 0.016. The training itself is sound; the failure is one of generalization.

GAR-Dongre provides a revealing control. Across both evaluation conditions, GAR-Dongre remains uniformly low (0.01--0.02) with no distribution gap. The distribution shift selectively destroys the concentrated attention pattern captured by GAR-ours (last-token, summary-position attention) while leaving the diffuse attention pattern captured by GAR-Dongre (averaged across all positions) unaffected. This selectivity implies that the distribution shift disrupts a specific learned routing behavior rather than attention computation in general.

The mechanism connecting training regime to distribution shift is exposure bias \citep{bengio2015scheduled}. During training, the model conditions each token prediction on ground-truth prefixes from UltraChat. At inference, it conditions on its own prior outputs. The attention patterns optimized for the former distribution do not transfer to the latter, because the statistical properties of model-generated text diverge from those of human-written reference text. The 2--7\% gate attenuation documented in \S\ref{subsec:gate-conditioning} is far too weak to compensate for this distributional mismatch.

\citet{he2019exposure} showed that language models exhibit token-level self-recovery from exposure bias: accumulated errors in autoregressive generation do not degrade perplexity as severely as worst-case analysis predicts. Our results are consistent with this finding at the token level, as PPL remains normal across all conditions (Table~\ref{tab:four-way}). The critical distinction is between primary and auxiliary objectives. The NTP objective is robust to exposure bias because next-token prediction is the same task at both training and inference time. The GAR auxiliary objective is fragile because it optimizes an attention pattern under teacher-forced context that has no counterpart in autoregressive generation. Primary-task self-recovery does not extend to auxiliary objectives that depend on distributional properties of the input prefix. Figure~\ref{fig:gate-shift}(b) summarizes the four-model GAR comparison across evaluation conditions.

      - "§2.4 Multi-task gradient conflict: GradNorm, PCGrad, CAGrad, Nash-MTL → 我们用 PCGrad 作因果分析工具而非优化工具"
      - "§2.5 Exposure bias: scheduled sampling, Professor Forcing, SEARNN → 现有文献聚焦 generation quality degradation，未涉及 auxiliary attention loss 泛化失败"
    dependencies: [introduction]

  - section: background
    word_budget: 350
    core_bullets:
      - "GAR 定义: 自包含 (不依赖 Dongre 才能理解)。Goal tokens G = system prompt task-specifying tokens。标注方式详述"
      - "两种 GAR 变体: GAR-Dongre (all response tokens, all layers/heads) vs GAR-ours (last token per assistant turn)"
      - "Residual stream persistence: Dongre probe AUC=0.98 → goal info 存在但 attention 通道关闭"
      - "问题陈述: 给定 GAR 衰减 + residual persistence，能否通过 residual gating 恢复 goal attention?"
    dependencies: []
    registry_refs: [phase1_gar_diag]

  - section: method
    word_budget: 750
    core_bullets:
      - "§4.1 ThreadGate 架构: per-layer sigmoid gate，正确公式 x_{l+1} = x_l + g_l · f_l(x_l) (ReZero-style, 非 Dream paper 的错误公式)"
      - "Gate 语义: g→0 = 子层输出被抑制 (层变 no-op)，g→1 = 保留完整子层计算"
      - "§4.2 Loss: L_total = L_NTP + λ_GAR·L_GAR + λ_div·L_div。L_GAR = MSE(GAR, target=0.5)，L_div = ReLU(min_std - std(g))"
      - "Loss 设计演化总结: v1-v7 覆盖 cumulative/maximize/smooth_saturation/mse_target 四种方案，MSE+gate_div 唯一收敛。详细表在 Appendix"
      - "§4.3 四路消融设计: ThreadGate (turn-conditioned) / Uniform Gate (content-only) / LoRA-only (gate=1.0) / Base → 隔离 turn conditioning 和 gating 本身的贡献"
      - "训练设置: Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, UltraChat 8K, 3 epochs, LoRA r=8, seed=42，所有 λ 值报告"
    dependencies: []
    tables: [tab_hyperparams]
    registry_refs: [phase2_tg_s42_v7, phase2_ug_s42, phase2_lora_only_s42]

  - section: experiments
    word_budget: 650
    core_bullets:
      - "§5.1 Setup: 4 models × 2 GAR metrics × 2 eval sets (IID overlap + held-out 50 convs no overlap) + PPL"
      - "§5.1 Main results (Table 1): TG/UG/LoRA-only GAR-ours ≈0.49-0.50 on ultrachat text，GAR-Dongre ~0.013-0.016，PPL ~2.63-2.78。Gating 零增量 (spread <0.75pp)"
      - "§5.1 Held-out validation: 三路趋同完全复现，排除数据重叠 confound"
      - "§5.1 Base model: GAR-ours ≈0.011, PPL=4.23 → LoRA fine-tuning 是 GAR recovery 唯一来源"
      - "§5.2 跨模型验证 Llama-3.1-8B [PLACEHOLDER: 待 C5 实验完成]"
    dependencies: [method, background]
    tables: [tab_main_results, tab_cross_model]
    registry_refs: [phase2_4way_eval, phase2_4way_eval_heldout, phase1_gar_diag]

  - section: analysis
    word_budget: 1000
    subsections:
      - name: "§6.1 Gradient Conflict Observation"
        word_budget: 200
        bullets:
          - "描述性 (非因果): 67-79% 层 NTP-GAR cos_sim<0，NTP magnitude 3-15x 压制 GAR"
          - "跨 epoch 演化: cos_sim -0.089→-0.042 (略缓解) 但 mag_ratio 7.5→14.7x (持续恶化)"
          - "明确标注: 这是观察而非因果 claim，为 §6.3 PCGrad 分析提供动机"
      - name: "§6.2 Gate Turn Conditioning"
        word_budget: 200
        bullets:
          - "27/28 层 gate diff (turn1 - turn21) < 0: 早期 turn 强抑制，晚期 turn passive (gate→1.0)"
          - "Wilcoxon signed-rank test p=3.73×10⁻⁸, effect size r=0.975"
          - "机制: NTP loss 梯度推 gate→1.0 以保留子层计算，晚期 turn NTP 压力最大"
          - "后果: gate 在需要干预处 (晚期 turn, 低 GAR) 反而最 passive——与设计意图完全相反"
      - name: "§6.3 PCGrad Causal Exclusion"
        word_budget: 300
        bullets:
          - "叙事结构: 观察 (§6.1) → 假设 (梯度方向冲突是 L_GAR 坍塌的因) → 实验排除 (PCGrad) → 修正假设 → 验证"
          - "PCGrad 机制: 投影 NTP 梯度到 GAR 梯度正交平面，消除方向冲突 (仅对 gate 参数)"
          - "结果: cos_sim 转正 (+0.086 at step 200)，但 L_GAR 坍塌轨迹不变 (仅延迟 ~350 步)"
          - "因果排除: 方向冲突被消除但结果不变 → 方向冲突是症状非原因"
          - "指向真因: distribution shift (exposure bias) — teacher-forced context 训练的 attention pattern 不迁移到 autoregressive generation context"
      - name: "§6.4 Distribution Shift Analysis"
        word_budget: 300
        bullets:
          - "Same-dist 泛化成功: 训练 GAR-ours=0.48 → ultrachat eval GAR-ours=0.49"
          - "Cross-dist 泛化失败: model-generated text GAR-ours=0.016 → 30x gap"
          - "选择性影响: GAR-Dongre 在两种分布上均低 (~0.01-0.016, 无 gap) → distribution shift 选择性破坏 summary-position (last token) attention pattern"
          - "连接 exposure bias 文献: teacher-forcing 训练 attention pattern 的泛化失败是 exposure bias 在 attention steering 场景的具体表现"
          - "推理时 gate attenuation 仅 2-7% (gate_mean=0.93-0.98) → 干预强度不足"
    dependencies: [experiments]
    tables: [tab_gradient_stats]
    figures: [fig2_training_pcgrad, fig3_gate_shift]
    registry_refs:
      - analysis_gradient_conflict
      - phase2_tg_s42_v7
      - phase2_tg_s42_v9_pcgrad
      - phase2_4way_eval
      - phase2_4way_eval_heldout
      - analysis_attention_heatmap

  - section: discussion
    word_budget: 400
    core_bullets:
      - "为什么 lightweight residual gating 不够: teacher-forcing 下 auxiliary attention loss 的 attention pattern 学习受 distribution shift 根本性制约"
      - "Constructive directions: (1) inference-time attention intervention 绕过训练泛化, (2) decoupled goal-processing pathway, (3) GAR-aware decoding 而非 GAR-aware training, (4) exposure bias mitigation (如 scheduled sampling) 应用于 auxiliary attention loss"
      - "与 Dongre convergent evidence: 两种独立干预路线 (goal re-injection + residual gating) 均失败 → lightweight intervention 在 NTP 压力下面临根本困难"
      - "Scope 声明: claim 限于 lightweight gating + GAR auxiliary loss，不泛化到所有 attention steering 方法"
    dependencies: [analysis]

  - section: conclusion
    word_budget: 200
    core_bullets:
      - "总结: 首个实证刻画 exposure bias 对 auxiliary attention loss 泛化性的破坏"
      - "核心数字: 30x training-inference GAR gap, 四路消融 gating 零增量, PCGrad 因果排除梯度冲突"
      - "对社区 actionable 建议: auxiliary attention loss 在 teacher-forcing 下有根本泛化障碍，建议探索 inference-time intervention 或 exposure bias mitigation"
    dependencies: [discussion]

  - section: limitations
    word_budget: 200
    core_bullets:
      - "单 seed (seed=42): held-out eval + bootstrap CI 提供统计支持但非多 seed 验证"
      - "单一 auxiliary loss type (GAR): 未测试其他 attention steering losses (如 head-specific 或 layer-specific attention loss)"
      - "训练数据规模: UltraChat 8K, 更大规模训练可能影响 gate dynamics"
      - "Llama-3 验证 [TODO if not done]: 跨模型泛化性需更多架构确认"
    dependencies: [experiments]

18	
19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	### 6.5 页面节奏
214	
215	好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：
216	
217	- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
218	- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
219	- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
220	- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
221	- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）
222	
223	### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范
224	
225	**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
226	- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
227	- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
228	- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
229	- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
230	- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）
231	
232	**宽度决策树**：
233	- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
234	- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
235	- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix
236	
237	---
238	
239	## 七、投稿前通用准备
240	
241	### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）
242	
243	- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
244	- **不要用**：
245	  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
246	  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
247	  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
248	- 风险：
249	  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
250	  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
251	  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
252	- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
253	- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致
254	
255	### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对
256	
257	- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
258	- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
259	- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
260	- 行号开启（review 版常需）
261	- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件
262	
263	### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程
264	
265	提交前必须逐一检查：
266	1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
267	2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
268	3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
269	4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
270	5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
271	6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
272	7. 所有专有名词有定义
273	8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
274	9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
275	10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础
276

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

### 3.3 禁忌

- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

### 4.2 结构要求

- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）

**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

### 5.2 段落与句式

- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容

### 5.3 用词黑名单

- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用

### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）

1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写

---

## 六、图表与视觉规范

### 6.1 知识密度原则

- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure

### 6.2 表格规范

- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
- 小数精度全表统一
- 最优加粗、次优下划线
- Caption 必须自包含

### 6.3 图片规范

- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页

### 6.4 空间效率

- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比

### 6.5 页面节奏

好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：

- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）

### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范

**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）

**宽度决策树**：
- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix

---

## 七、投稿前通用准备

### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）

- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
- **不要用**：
  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
- 风险：
  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致

### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对

- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
- 行号开启（review 版常需）
- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件

### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程

提交前必须逐一检查：
1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
7. 所有专有名词有定义
8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

你需要为论文 "Why Lightweight Gating Fails to Fix Multi-Turn Attention Degradation: A Mechanistic Analysis" 撰写 Introduction 章节（§1），目标 venue 是 EMNLP 2026（ARR August cycle），8 页正文限制。

## 必读规范

**开始写作前必须先 Read 以下两个 skill 文件：**
1. `Read /home/ubuntu/agent-ml-research/skills/global/paper-writing-norms.skill.md`

## 章节规格

- **Word budget**: ~850 words
- **文件路径**: `/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/introduction.tex`

## 叙事结构（5 段 + 贡献列表）

### 第 1 段：Hook + 问题（研究背景）
- Multi-turn dialogue 是 LLM 最普遍的使用场景
- System prompt 中的 goal specification 是 instruction-following 的基础
- Dongre et al. (2026) 量化了这个问题：12 个模型上 GAR 平均下降 70.8%（我们在 Qwen-2.5-7B 上验证：turn 1 GAR=0.0418 → mid-turn GAR=0.0122）
- 引用：`\citet{dongre2026attention}`

### 第 2 段：关键观察 + 自然假说
- Dongre et al. 的关键发现：goal info 在 residual stream 中持续存在（LDA probe AUC=0.98），即使 attention 已衰减
- 信息可用但不被利用 → 自然假说：learnable residual gate 可以恢复 goal attention
- 这导向了 ThreadGate 的设计：per-layer sigmoid gate x_{l+1} = x_l + g_l · f_l(x_l)

### 第 3 段：方法概述
- ThreadGate：per-layer learnable sigmoid gate，联合 NTP + auxiliary GAR loss (MSE target) + gate diversity loss
- 系统化设计：v1-v7 覆盖 4 种 loss formulation（cumulative, maximize, smooth saturation, MSE target），MSE+gate_div 是唯一收敛方案
- 四路消融：ThreadGate / Uniform Gate / LoRA-only / Base，隔离 gating 贡献

### 第 4 段：惊喜失败 + 机制发现
- 训练成功：GAR 从 0.02 升至 0.48（在训练分布上）
- Same-distribution 泛化成功：held-out teacher-forced GAR=0.49-0.50
- **30x 断层**：model-generated text GAR 仅 0.016
- 四路消融确认 gating 零增量：ThreadGate/Uniform Gate/LoRA-only 在 GAR-ours 上 spread 仅 0.75pp，PPL 完全一致（2.78）
- 机制因果链：观察梯度冲突（68-79% 层 cos_sim<0）→ PCGrad 消除方向冲突 → L_GAR 仍坍塌 → 排除梯度冲突为因 → 指向 distribution shift（exposure bias）

### 第 5 段：Contributions（编号列表）
1. 首个实证刻画 exposure bias 如何破坏 auxiliary attention loss 的泛化性：training-inference GAR gap 达 30x
2. PCGrad 因果排除实验建立完整因果链：梯度方向冲突是症状而非原因
3. ThreadGate + 系统化四路消融为 residual gating 在 multi-turn attention recovery 中提供 principled negative baseline
4. 跨模型验证（Llama-3.1-8B，如 §5.3 placeholder）
